title: Boxes and Bushes
checkpoint: Year 1 Summer 2, week 4 — School readiness — Phase 6: new sounds -er, -est
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 6 book for making words mean more than one. Most words just add '-s'; words ending in x, s, ch and sh add '-es' so you can still say them (box → boxes). Count the boxes on the last page together.

pages.text: Moss had six boxes. The boxes were for nuts, and all six were still not full.
pages.illustration: Moss the berry-brown hedgehog beside six battered wooden crates on the grass, all clearly empty, one on its side. He is peering hopefully into the nearest. Dewy morning light.

pages.text: Nell said she had seen the best bushes. She said they had hundreds of nuts.
pages.illustration: Nell the bee hovering with both front legs flung wide in an exaggerated 'this many' gesture. Moss looking sceptical. Sunflower yellow against deep green.

pages.text: The bushes had five nuts. Nell said she had said five hundred.
pages.illustration: A thin scrubby bush bearing exactly five nuts, drawn precisely so they can be counted. Nell hovering a bit lower now, sheepish. Moss entirely deadpan.

pages.text: So they went to the big bushes. The bushes had branches, and the branches had nuts.
pages.illustration: A tall dense bush filling the page, heavy with nuts, drawn in loving detail. Moss at the bottom looking up with his mouth open. Rich saturated greens and browns.

pages.text: They picked and picked. The boxes got fuller and the bushes got barer.
pages.illustration: Two panels side by side from the same viewpoint: left, the crates filling up; right, the same branch stripped and springing back. The change reads instantly.

pages.text: Olive got out the dishes. She said nuts in boxes go soft, but nuts in dishes do not.
pages.illustration: Olive the owl arriving importantly with two chipped china dishes balanced on her wings. Moss and Nell exchanging a look. Comic gravitas.

pages.text: They filled the dishes. Then they filled the boxes. Then they filled Moss.
pages.illustration: Moss sitting among the crates with an enormously round tummy and one last nut in his paw. Nell and Olive either side of him. Very funny.

pages.text: “Next time,” said Olive, “we get bigger boxes.”
pages.illustration: Closing page: the three walking home at dusk, Nell towing one dish, Olive carrying the other, Moss rolling along behind like a nut himself. Warm purple evening sky.
